questions.subject: MATH
questions.learningObjective: Solve problems involving euler and hamilton circuits.
questions.stem: Consider the following: how many separate Hamiltonian cycles does the complete network K_5 have, counting rotations and reversals as the same?

options.misconception: Wrong belief "identifies rotations but not reversals" gives 24, not 12.
Wrong belief "fixes no starting vertex" gives 60, not 12.
Wrong belief "fixes two vertices unnecessarily" gives 3, not 12.

questions.explanation: Fix a start vertex, arrange the other 4 vertices in (5-1) factorial ways, then divide by 2 because each cycle is traced in two directions, giving 12.
questions.hint: Fix a start and divide by two for the two directions.

questions.stem: Under this scenario, a connected graph has exactly 10 points of odd degree. What is the minimum number of trails needed to cover every edge exactly once?

options.misconception: Wrong belief "uses one trail per odd vertex" gives 10, not 5.
Wrong belief "adds a spurious extra trail" gives 6, not 5.
Wrong belief "miscounts the pairing of odd vertices" gives 11, not 5.

questions.explanation: Odd-degree vertices can be paired up, and each pair needs one trail, so 10 odd vertices require 5 trails to cover all edges.
questions.hint: Pair the odd vertices; each pair accounts for one trail.
